quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud and make the vowels clearly different.
quests.hint: 'sit' and 'still' have the short vowel [ɪ]; 'these' and 'seats' have the long vowel [iː].
quests.explanation: For [iː], spread your lips as if smiling, raise the tongue high and hold the vowel. For [ɪ], relax the lips and jaw slightly and keep the vowel short.
quests.textToSpeak: I can't sit still; these seats are too hard.
quests.phoneticHint: 'seat' [siːt] versus 'sit' [sɪt]: [iː] is tense and long, [ɪ] is relaxed and short.
commonMistakes: Saying 'sit' with [iː], so it sounds like 'seat'
Tensing the lips too much on [ɪ]

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a clinic receptionist.
quests.hint: 'feel' and 'leave' use [iː]; 'ill', 'fill', 'in', 'this' and 'it' use [ɪ]. 'reception' starts with a weak [ɪ].
quests.explanation: Lengthen [iː] in 'feel' and 'leave' and end cleanly on [l] or [v]. Keep [ɪ] short and loose in 'ill' and 'fill'.
quests.textToSpeak: If you feel ill, fill in this form and leave it at reception.
commonMistakes: Saying the first syllable of 'reception' with [iː]

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a workplace scheduling comment.
quests.explanation: In 'meeting', the stressed first syllable has the long [iː] and the second syllable [ɪŋ] is short. Make that contrast clear.
quests.textToSpeak: Chris and I need to meet at six, but the meeting might finish late.
quests.phoneticHint: 'meeting' is [ˈmiːtɪŋ]: long then short. 'Chris' is [krɪs], 'six' is [sɪks], and 'finish' is [ˈfɪnɪʃ].
commonMistakes: Making both vowels of 'meeting' equally long

quests.instruction: Read it aloud, giving each vowel in [e] vs [ɪ] its full length and shape.
quests.explanation: For [e], open the jaw a little more than for [ɪ] and let the tongue sit lower at the front. [ɪ] is more closed and relaxed.
quests.textToSpeak: The letter is in the red bin, not on the table.
commonMistakes: Adding a glide to [e] so it becomes [eɪ]

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a quick check on a colleague.
quests.explanation: 'message' has [e] then a weak [ɪ] in the last syllable: keep the first vowel clear and the last one short and reduced.
quests.textToSpeak: Did you get my message? I sent it yesterday.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would in an office.
quests.explanation: Move between the two vowels by adjusting jaw height only: slightly more open for [e], more closed and relaxed for [ɪ]. Don't change the lips.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not sure this printer will fit next to the desk, but let's check.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a polite request.
quests.explanation: For [æ], open the jaw wide and drop the tongue low at the front, lips neutral. For [e], the jaw closes about halfway.
quests.textToSpeak: Can you lend me a pen? I left my bag at the bank.
commonMistakes: Not opening the jaw enough for [æ]

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a sick-day message.
quests.explanation: 'had' and 'head' differ mostly in jaw opening: wide for [æ], half-open for [e]. The vowel in 'bad' is often slightly longer than in 'had'.
quests.textToSpeak: I had a bad headache, so I said I'd stay in bed.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a workplace request Watch the [æ] vs [e].
quests.explanation: Alternate jaw positions cleanly: wide for [æ] in 'attach' and 'map', half-open for [e] in 'let', 'send' and 'rest'.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you attach the map, and let me know when you send the rest?

quests.instruction: Read it aloud, giving each vowel in [ʌ] its full length and shape.
quests.hint: The letter o gives [ʌ] in 'husband', 'loves', 'son' and 'doesn't'. Spelling won't help here.
quests.explanation: For [ʌ], keep the mouth half-open, lips relaxed, tongue low and central. It is short, and quite unlike the rounded [oʊ].
quests.textToSpeak: My husband loves football, but my son doesn't.
commonMistakes: Reading o as [oʊ], so 'loves' sounds like 'loaves'
Rounding the lips so 'son' sounds like 'sawn'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would describe a relative.
quests.explanation: For [ɑː], drop the jaw fully and pull the tongue back, and hold the vowel. [ʌ] is shorter, with less jaw opening.
quests.textToSpeak: My uncle is a farmer; he starts work before dawn.
commonMistakes: Saying 'starts' with [ʌ], so it sounds like 'stuts'
Saying 'uncle' with a rounded vowel, like 'ong-kle'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would tell a colleague.
quests.explanation: Three jaw positions: half-open and short for [ʌ], fully open and long for [ɑː], wide and forward for [æ]. Feel the jaw open a bit more each time.
quests.textToSpeak: Hang on. I have to run to the market and get some fruit.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a shop manager's update.
quests.explanation: For [ɔː], round the lips clearly and hold the vowel, tongue pulled back. For [ɒ], the mouth opens more and the vowel is shorter. American English usually says [ɑː] where British has [ɒ].
quests.textToSpeak: The shop is short of stock, but the boss says it's not a problem.
commonMistakes: Making 'short' too short, so it sounds like 'shot'
Rounding [ɒ] too much, so 'shop' sounds like 'shawp'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as workplace news.
quests.explanation: Round and hold the lips for 'Paul' and 'called', then relax into the shorter vowel in 'office' and 'lost'.
quests.textToSpeak: Paul called from the office; he's lost the report.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a casual explanation.
quests.explanation: 'wash' takes [ɒ], though many learners expect [æ]; 'all' and 'morning' need rounded, held lips.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't wash up because I was on the phone all morning.

quests.instruction: Read it aloud, giving each vowel in [ʊ] vs [uː] its full length and shape.
quests.hint: 'took', 'good', 'look', 'full' and 'books' use short [ʊ]; 'room' and 'cool' use long [uː].
quests.explanation: For [uː], round and push the lips forward and hold the vowel. For [ʊ], the lips are rounded but relaxed and the vowel is short.
quests.textToSpeak: I took a good look at the room. It's cool, but it's full of books.
commonMistakes: Saying 'full' with [uː], so it sounds like 'fool'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a shopping tip.
quests.hint: 'you', 'choose', 'blue' and 'too' use long [uː]; 'should', 'wool' and 'look' use short [ʊ].
quests.explanation: Make the lips tighter and more pushed out for [uː]. Keep [ʊ] relaxed and brief.
quests.textToSpeak: You should choose the blue ones; the wool ones look too soft.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a question in a meeting.
quests.explanation: Alternate between relaxed rounding and pushed-out rounding: [ʊ] for 'pull' and 'put', [uː] for 'rules', 'who', 'group' and 'two'.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you pull up the rules? I'd like to know who put us in Group Two.

quests.instruction: Read it aloud, giving each vowel in [ɜː] its full length and shape.
quests.hint: The spellings 'er', 'ir', 'or' and 'ur' all give [ɜː] in 'her', 'first', 'work' and 'worse'.
quests.explanation: For [ɜː], keep the lips relaxed and unrounded, the tongue central, and hold the vowel. In r-pronouncing accents, bunch the tongue for the r-colouring.
quests.textToSpeak: Her first day at work was worse than she expected.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lips, so 'work' sounds like 'walk'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud at a dinner table.
quests.explanation: Hold [ɜː] in the stressed syllables: 'turn', 'serve', 'prefer'. In 'dessert' the vowel is in the second, stressed syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: It's my turn to serve dessert; I'd prefer the cherry pie.
quests.phoneticHint: 'dessert' is [dɪˈzɜːrt] with stress on the second syllable; 'prefer' is [prɪˈfɜːr]; 'cherry' [ˈtʃeri] uses [e].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a traveller.
quests.explanation: Neither 'ear' nor 'ur' should sound like 'air' or 'eer'. The 'ear' in 'heard' and 'earlier' is a plain [ɜː].
quests.textToSpeak: I heard the earlier service was cancelled, so we'll be late.
quests.phoneticHint: 'heard' is [hɜːrd], the same as 'herd'; 'earlier' is [ˈɜːrliər]; 'service' is [ˈsɜːrvɪs].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud and let the weak syllables be quick.
quests.hint: The first syllable of 'around' and 'about', and the word 'a', all contain a weak vowel.
quests.explanation: Schwa is the weakest vowel: relax the tongue, jaw and lips completely and say it very short and quiet. It occurs only in unstressed syllables.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's meet around seven, about a minute from the station.
quests.phoneticHint: 'around' is [əˈraʊnd], 'about' is [əˈbaʊt], and 'a' is [ə]. The stress falls on 'round' and 'bout'.
commonMistakes: Saying the first syllable of 'around' with a full [æ] or [ɑː]
Saying the article 'a' as [eɪ] in the middle of a phrase

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a health-worker update.
quests.explanation: In 'customer' the last two syllables are both weak [ə]; in 'pharmacist' the middle vowel is a schwa. Don't say each vowel as it is spelled.
quests.textToSpeak: The pharmacist gave the customer a leaflet about the medicine.
commonMistakes: Giving each syllable of 'customer' equal weight

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would order at a café.
quests.hint: The small words 'can', 'a', 'of' and 'and' get weak vowels here.
quests.explanation: Function words are usually spoken in their weak forms: 'a' [ə], 'of' [əv], 'and' [ən], 'can' [kən]. The nouns 'cup', 'tea', 'piece' and 'cake' carry the stress.
quests.textToSpeak: Can I have a cup of tea and a piece of cake?
quests.phoneticHint: [kən aɪ ˈhæv ə ˈkʌp əv ˈtiː ən ə ˈpiːs əv ˈkeɪk]: weak syllables squeeze between strong ones.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a short story.
quests.hint: Every stressed word here ends on the glide [eɪ]: 'rained', 'day', 'stayed', 'played' and 'games'.
quests.explanation: [eɪ] starts in the middle of the mouth and glides toward [ɪ]. Both halves count: don't stop at [e], and don't overdo the glide.
quests.textToSpeak: It rained all day, so we stayed in and played games.
quests.phoneticHint: 'day' is [deɪ], 'rained' is [reɪnd], and 'games' is [geɪmz]: the vowel ends with the tongue rising.
commonMistakes: Making it a flat [e], so 'games' sounds like 'gems'
Stretching the glide until it sounds like [aɪ]

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would think out loud.
quests.hint: 'wait' and 'late' use the glide [eɪ]; 'let' and 'check' use the plain [e].
quests.explanation: [e] is a single, steady vowel with no glide. [eɪ] moves. The difference is the tongue rising toward the top of the mouth.
quests.textToSpeak: Wait, let me check my diary; I think we're late.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as you would in a customer-service chat.
quests.hint: 'payment', 'failed', 'change', 'date' and 'pay' all use [eɪ]. 'Monday' ends with [eɪ] too.
quests.explanation: In 'payment' the [eɪ] is in the stressed first syllable and the glide is short. At the end of 'pay' and 'Monday', finish with a clear high glide.
quests.textToSpeak: The payment failed, so I'll change the date and pay on Monday.

quests.instruction: Read it aloud, giving each vowel in [aɪ] its full length and shape.
quests.explanation: [aɪ] starts with the jaw wide open and glides up toward [ɪ]. Make both parts audible; the first is louder and longer.
quests.textToSpeak: I might try the pie; it looks nice.
quests.phoneticHint: 'try' is [traɪ], 'might' is [maɪt], and 'nice' is [naɪs]: start low, finish high.
commonMistakes: Flattening it to [a] and dropping the glide
Turning it into [eɪ], so 'nice' sounds like 'nace'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a travel update.
quests.explanation: Start [aɪ] with a wide-open jaw and [eɪ] with a half-open jaw. The starting point is the difference; both end high.
quests.textToSpeak: My flight arrives at nine, but the pilot said we might be delayed.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a shopper deciding.
quests.explanation: 'high' and 'buy' end with the glide, so finish on a clear [ɪ] position; before a consonant, as in 'white', the vowel is a little shorter.
quests.textToSpeak: Should I buy the white one or the silver? I like both, but the price is high.
quests.phoneticHint: 'buy' is [baɪ], 'white' is [waɪt], 'price' is [praɪs], and 'high' is [haɪ]; 'silver' is [ˈsɪlvər], with [ɪ].
